cover.headline: India's best pharma franchise, about to become half of a bigger, slower and indebted company
cover.lead: Sun is India's largest drugmaker (8.5% of the market), the 13th largest US generics company and, with $1.42 bn of sales from Ilumya, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt and 26 other branded products, the only Indian company with a real global specialty business. On 27-Apr-2026 it agreed to buy **Organon & Co. for an enterprise value of $11.75 bn**, doubling revenue and taking on ~$9.5 bn of net debt; the deal was still awaiting regulatory approvals on 30-Sep-2026 (closing guided for Q4FY27). The street values Sun on **P/E on 12-month-forward or FY28E earnings**. We forecast standalone EPS of ₹51.3 / ₹58.4 / ₹65.2 for FY27-29E, ~8-11% below the street (higher tax, no forex gains, slower US). On the house rule (Sun's 26.6x median forward P/E on adjusted EPS × the +10.25% pharma factor = **29.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹61.8**) plus Organon at what Sun pays (−₹26.2 a share), our target is **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: India and innovative medicines carry the growth
arguments.p: India grew 16% in Q1FY27 (volume +5.4% vs the market's +2%) and Sun's share rose to 8.5% from 8.2%; it is No.1 by prescriptions with 12 specialist groups and No.2 in the new generic semaglutide market. Innovative medicines grew from $674 mn in FY22 to $1,420 mn in FY26 (Ilumya $796 mn) and $351 mn in Q1FY27 (+13%); Ilumya's US decision in psoriatic arthritis is due in late Oct-2026. Together they are ~55% of sales and most of the profit growth.

arguments.h: US generics shrink, and the plants are the reason
arguments.p: US sales fell 9.7% to $427 mn in Q1FY27 as gRevlimid ended and competition rose; they have been ~$1.9 bn for three years. Four Indian plants are under FDA action (Halol import alert since 2022, Mohali under consent-decree batch checks, Dadra warning letter, Baska OAI since Dec-2025) and the chairman admits Sun is not getting approvals. From 29-Sep-2026 patented imports into the US carry a 100% Section 232 tariff unless exempt; Sun calls the FY27 impact marginal.

arguments.h: Organon: accretive on paper, not obviously valuable
arguments.p: Sun pays 6.2x EBITDA and ~4x adjusted earnings for a company whose revenue fell 3% in 2025 and again in H1-2026, so the street sees 30-40% EPS accretion by FY28. But the earnings come with ~2.3x net debt/EBITDA, falling Nexplanon and China sales and only a third of the portfolio growing. A P/E built on Sun's own history should not be applied to Organon's earnings. We value Organon at cost: no value created until the $350 mn of synergies show.

At ₹1,817 the stock trades at 31.1x our FY28E EPS. Its forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of 26.6x on adjusted EPS (29.1x on reported EPS); peers trade 10% above their five-year medians, so the house multiple is 29.5x. That gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, below the post-results street median of ₹2,100. The gap is mostly earnings: we are ~10% below the street on FY28E EPS (₹58.4 vs ~₹66.2).

catalysts: US FDA decision on Ilumya in psoriatic arthritis (action date late Oct-2026): the biggest near-term lever for innovative-medicine growth.
Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the US generics base after gRevlimid, R&D returning to 6-7% of sales, Organon deal costs, the tax rate.

Organon closing (guided Q4FY27, i.e. Jan-Mar 2027): remaining regulatory approvals, the financing (bonds vs bank debt, cost), the dividend policy and the purchase-price allocation that will set reported EPS.
Section 232 tariffs on patented drug imports, in force for most companies from 29-Sep-2026: how Sun sources Ilumya, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt and its other branded products for the US.
FDA re-inspections of Halol, Baska and Dadra; new US generic approvals; AbbVie's Rinvoq decision in alopecia areata (expected by early 2027) against Leqselvi.

sections.title: Four businesses of similar size, and a global specialty arm that runs through three of them

blocks.p: Sun makes and sells medicines in 100+ countries from 40 plants. Its FY26 gross sales of ₹58,220 cr came from five lines: **India formulations** (₹19,290 cr, 33%; branded generics sold through ~16,800 medical representatives), **US formulations** (₹16,824 cr, 29%; $1.9 bn, now more than half innovative medicines, the rest generics incl. Taro), **Emerging Markets** (₹11,187 cr, 19%; branded generics in 80+ countries, focus on Romania, Russia, South Africa, Brazil and Mexico), **Rest of World** (₹8,568 cr, 15%; Western Europe, Canada, Japan, Australia, Israel) and **API** (₹2,185 cr, 4%). Cutting across the US, RoW and EM is the **innovative medicines** business: 29 branded products in dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology, $1,420 mn of sales in FY26 (22% of the total), led by the psoriasis biologic Ilumya ($796 mn).

blocks.callout: **So what:** Sun is not one business but a portfolio. India (33.0% of FY27E revenue in our build) is a high-margin, steady compounder; innovative medicines are the growth engine and the reason Sun trades at a premium to generic peers; US generics, once the core, are now a shrinking, low-margin drag held back by factory problems. Organon would add a fifth, larger piece: mature off-patent brands, women's health and biosimilars.

sections.title: Built by acquisition: Caraco, Taro, Ranbaxy, then specialty assets, now Organon

blocks.p: Dilip Shanghvi started Sun in 1983 with five psychiatry products and ₹10,000 of capital. Its rise has been a sequence of acquisitions, mostly of troubled assets bought cheaply and fixed: Caraco (US entry, 1997), Taro (2010), DUSA (2012), Ranbaxy (2015, all-stock) and a string of specialty products in 2014-25. Organon (2026) is the largest by far and the first funded with heavy debt.

blocks.callout: **The pattern to remember:** Sun's best deals were cheap and small relative to the company (Taro, DUSA, Ilumya's licence, Concert). Ranbaxy was large, took five years to fix (Halol and Mohali still carry its legacy) and diluted shareholders ~15%. Organon is Ranbaxy-sized, but paid in cash and debt, so the dilution risk is replaced by a leverage risk.

sections.title: Three different markets: a growing Indian branded market, a deflating US generics market and a niche specialty market

blocks.h: India: ₹2.5 lakh crore, growing ~10% a year, fragmented

blocks.p: The Indian pharmaceutical market was ₹2,52,700 cr in the 12 months to Jun-2026 (Pharmarack). Growth is mostly price and new products; volume grew only ~2% in Q1FY27. The market is fragmented: the top 12 companies hold ~54%. Sun leads with 8.5%, ahead of Abbott (5.9%), Cipla (5.8%) and Mankind (5.5%). Chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, neuro, gastro) grow faster than acute ones and are where Sun is strongest. GLP-1 generics (semaglutide went off patent in India in Mar-2026) pushed diabetes growth to ~15%.

blocks.h: US generics: volume grows, prices fall every year

blocks.p: US generics are a commodity market: buying groups negotiate hard, each new competitor cuts prices, and growth comes only from new approvals and limited-competition launches (such as gRevlimid in 2022-26). Sun is the 13th largest player, with 558 approved ANDAs and 119 pending (Jun-2026), but its Indian plants' FDA problems have slowed approvals. From 29-Sep-2026 the US charges a 100% Section 232 tariff on imported **patented** drugs (15% for the EU and Japan, 0% for companies with pricing-and-onshoring agreements); **generics and biosimilars are excluded**, for now: the Commerce Department must report within a year on whether to extend them.

blocks.h: Specialty: dermatology, ophthalmology, onco-derm; women's health and biosimilars with Organon

blocks.p: Sun's innovative medicines compete in niches: IL-23 biologics in psoriasis (Ilumya vs J&J's Tremfya and AbbVie's Skyrizi, and cheap Stelara biosimilars), JAK inhibitors in alopecia (Leqselvi vs Lilly's Olumiant, Pfizer's Litfulo and soon AbbVie's Rinvoq), PD-1/PD-L1 drugs in skin cancer (Unloxcyt vs Libtayo and Keytruda). Organon would add women's health (a $35 bn market growing 6-10%, Organon No.2 in contraception, No.3 in fertility) and biosimilars ($320 bn of drugs lose exclusivity by 2035, a ~$70 bn biosimilar opportunity per Sun).

blocks.callout: **So what:** two of Sun's three markets are attractive (India branded, global specialty). The third (US generics) is structurally deflationary and needs a clean factory record, which Sun currently lacks in India.

sections.title: $1.42 bn of specialty sales, growing ~13-17%; the new launches are slower than hoped

blocks.p: Sun began building a branded ("innovative" or "specialty") business in 2012 with DUSA's Levulan and now sells 29 such products, mostly in the US through its own sales force. Sales grew from $674 mn in FY22 to $1,420 mn in FY26 (+16.8% in FY26) and were $351 mn in Q1FY27 (+12.8%, 21.9% of Sun's sales). In the US, innovative medicines passed $1 bn in FY26 and are now bigger than Sun's US generics. The engine is **Ilumya** (tildrakizumab, an IL-23 biologic for psoriasis licensed from Merck in 2014): $796 mn in FY26 (+16.7%), launched in ~40 countries, with a US decision on psoriatic arthritis due in late Oct-2026. Behind it come Cequa (dry eye), Odomzo (basal cell carcinoma), Winlevi (acne) and Levulan, and two launches: **Leqselvi** (oral JAK for severe alopecia areata; US launch 14-Jul-2025 after a royalty-bearing settlement with Incyte) and **Unloxcyt** (PD-L1 antibody for advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; available from 15-Jan-2026).

blocks.p: Three questions decide this business. (1) **Can Ilumya keep growing?** IL-23 is the fastest-growing class in psoriasis, and Ilumya's Medicare Part B channel is not affected by cheap Stelara biosimilars (management), but it is the third IL-23 in a market led by J&J's Tremfya and AbbVie's Skyrizi; psoriatic arthritis (decision late Oct-2026) adds a second indication. (2) **How fast do Leqselvi and Unloxcyt build?** Management will not give product numbers; Leqselvi passed 1,000 prescribers in June 2026 and has most US covered lives, Unloxcyt is being added to cancer-centre formularies. But global innovative sales were broadly flat for three quarters despite both launches (an analyst's point on the Q1 call), launch spend (~$100 mn in FY26) is now permanent, and AbbVie's Rinvoq could be approved in alopecia by early 2027. (3) **Can Sun replace products that lose exclusivity?** The in-house pipeline is thin (Fibromun in Phase 3, Nidlegy refiled in Europe by its partner, GL0034 and MM-II to be partnered; SCD-044 was dropped in FY26).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** a valuable, profitable franchise (we estimate it earns well above the group margin) that has moved Sun from a generics company to a hybrid. But it is mid-sized by global standards ($1.4 bn), built on in-licensed molecules with limited patent life, and its growth is slowing from 20%+ to low-to-mid teens. We do not model it separately; our US dollar growth of −4% / +6% / +6% assumes innovative medicines grow ~12-15% a year and offset generic erosion from FY28.

sections.title: US: $1.9 bn for three years, falling in FY27; four plants under FDA action

blocks.p: US formulations were $1,921 mn in FY25, $1,905 mn in FY26 and $427 mn in Q1FY27 (−9.7%; 26.6% of sales). The mix has changed: innovative medicines grew to over $1 bn while generics (including Taro, fully owned since Jun-2024) shrank, first through price erosion and then through the end of gRevlimid (the limited-volume generic of Revlimid that boosted many Indian companies in FY23-26 until full generic entry in Jan-2026). Management blames "additional competition in certain products" and, more fundamentally, the plants: "because of the compliance issue, we haven't been getting approval" (chairman, 22-May-2026).

blocks.h: Tariffs: generics are exempt; patented products are not

blocks.p: Section 232 proclamation of 2-Apr-2026 (Proclamation 11020): 100% duty on patented pharmaceuticals and their APIs (15% for EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland; 10% UK; 20% for companies with approved US onshoring plans; 0% to Jan-2029 for companies with MFN-pricing and onshoring agreements); generics and biosimilars excluded (Commerce to review within a year); orphan drugs can get 0%. In force from 31-Jul-2026 for companies named in Annex III and from 29-Sep-2026 for all others. Sun has three US formulation plants (Levulan is made in the US); it does not disclose where Ilumya, Cequa, Odomzo, Winlevi, Leqselvi or Unloxcyt are made. Its North America CEO called the FY27 impact "marginal" (22-May-2026) and said Sun is looking at all alternatives. We model no tariff cost; it is a risk to our innovative growth assumption if Sun has to absorb the duty on a large product.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** US generics are a drag, not a driver, and will remain so until Halol, Mohali, Dadra and Baska are cleared; the greenfield sterile plant in Madhya Pradesh is years away. We assume US dollar sales fall 4% in FY27E (gRevlimid out of the base; Q1 annualises at ~$1.71 bn) and grow 6% a year in FY28-29E on innovative medicines. Street estimates (Emkay: US ~$1.9 bn for a third year) are similar.

sections.title: India: No.1 and still gaining share; the most valuable part of Sun

blocks.p: India formulations grew 14% to ₹19,290 cr in FY26 and 16% to ₹5,475 cr in Q1FY27 (36% of sales). Sun's share of the Indian market rose from 8.1% to 8.4% in FY26, "the highest gain since the Ranbaxy acquisition" (MD), and to 8.5% in the 12 months to Jun-2026. Growth is unusually volume-led: in Q1FY27 40% came from volume and 20% from new products (volume +5.4% vs the market's +2%), helped by field-force expansion into tier-2 and tier-3 towns (medical reps up from 11,149 in FY22 to 16,767 in FY26) while productivity held at ₹11.5 mn per rep, the industry's highest. Sun is No.1 by prescriptions with 12 groups of specialists, has 30 brands in India's top 300 and its top 10 brands are only ~17% of India sales. Semaglutide (launched 21-Mar-2026 as Noveltreat and Sematrinity, with the only auto-injector) made Sun the No.2 generic player within four months.

sections.title: EM and RoW: a third of sales, growing high single digits in dollars; currency flatters the rupee numbers

blocks.p: **Emerging Markets** (₹11,187 cr, 19% of FY26 sales) are branded generics sold by ~3,300 reps in 80+ countries, with local plants in Bangladesh, South Africa, Malaysia, Romania, Egypt, Nigeria, Morocco and Russia. FY26 sales were $1,265 mn (+13.6%; +8.2% in constant currency); Q1FY27 $311 mn, only +4.2%, which management put down to "geopolitical issues and difficult macroeconomic conditions in certain countries". Ilumya is now sold in several EMs (Romania, Brazil) and semaglutide is approved in South Africa (launched) and Brazil (partner launch due). **Rest of World** (₹8,568 cr, 15%) covers Western Europe, Canada, Japan, Australia and Israel: $969 mn in FY26 (+14.4%, led by Ilumya and Odomzo), but flat at $218 mn for two quarters. **API** (₹2,185 cr, 4%) supplies Sun's own formulations and third parties from 13 sites.

sections.title: Organon: Sun doubles in size for $11.75 bn; cheap on earnings, expensive on what it does to the balance sheet

blocks.p: On 27-Apr-2026 Sun signed a definitive agreement to buy **Organon & Co.** (NYSE: OGN), the women's-health, biosimilars and established-brands company spun out of Merck in 2021, for **$14.00 a share in cash: equity value $3.99 bn, enterprise value $11.75 bn**. Organon's shareholders approved it in July 2026; regulatory filings were complete and some approvals received by 31-Jul-2026; closing is guided for Q4FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027). Sun will pay $2.0-2.5 bn from its own cash and the rest with committed bank debt, and inherit Organon's ~$8.5 bn of debt. FY2025: revenue $6,216 mn (-3%): women's health $1,752 mn (Nexplanon $921 mn), biosimilars $691 mn (Hadlima, Renflexis; +13% CAGR since 2021), established brands $3,691 mn (Zetia, Atozet, Arcoxia, Hyzaar, Cozaar, Singulair), other $82 mn; adjusted EBITDA $1,907 mn (30.7%); GAAP net income $187 mn; adjusted net income $954 mn (EPS $3.66); debt $8.64 bn, cash $574 mn at Dec-2025. 2026 guidance: revenue ~$6.2 bn, adjusted EBITDA ~$1.9 bn, interest ~$500 mn. Q2-2026 (10-Q, Aug-2026): revenue $1.56 bn (-2%), H1 $3.02 bn (-3%); Nexplanon down, stabilisation expected in H2-2026; China volume-based procurement and LOEs weigh. China sales >$800 mn.

blocks.h: How we treat Organon in the valuation

blocks.p: Our forecasts are **standalone Sun**: the deal had not closed by 30-Sep-2026, management gives no Organon guidance, and the multiple we derive comes from Sun's own history and pharma peers, so applying it to Organon's earnings would be wrong (it would capitalise earnings bought at ~4x at ~29.5x). We add Organon as a separate part of the sum: **valued at what Sun pays** (6.2x EBITDA, close to ICICI Securities' 6x), so the deal itself creates or destroys nothing in our base case. One adjustment remains: the ~$2.25 bn of cash that leaves Sun earns interest that sits inside our standalone EPS (₹3.9 a share after tax), and the P/E multiple values it at ₹116 a share, while it is worth only its face value of ₹90. The difference, **−₹26.2 a share**, comes off. In the bull case we add the $350 mn of cost synergies at the deal multiple, discounted two years (₹69.5 a share); in the bear case we take off a 10% shortfall in Organon's $1.9 bn EBITDA at the same multiple (₹46.7 a share).

sections.title: R&D at 6% of sales, a third of it on innovation; the in-house pipeline is thin

blocks.p: Sun spent ₹3,554 cr on R&D in FY26 (6.1% of sales; ₹33,500 cr cumulatively since inception) through 2,700+ scientists. About 39% of FY26 R&D went to innovative medicines (30% in Q1FY27), the rest to generics for the US, India and other markets. Guidance for FY27 is 6-7% of sales; Q1 was 5.4% because some trials ended before new ones started. The innovative pipeline has one near-term event (Ilumya in psoriatic arthritis) and few new molecules; Sun's strategy is to in-license or buy late-stage assets (Ilumya, Winlevi, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt all came from outside) and partner early ones in big markets.

sections.title: Revenue up 75% in five years; margins up 3 points; reported profit dented by a charge every year

blocks.p: Sun's consolidated revenue went from ₹33,498 cr in FY21 to ₹58,462 cr in FY26: 11.8% a year. EBITDA before forex gains rose from ₹8,470 cr to ₹16,501 cr and the margin from 25.3% to 28.2%, as innovative medicines grew from 13% of sales in FY22 to 22% in FY26 and India kept gaining share. Reported EPS looks volatile (₹12.1 in FY21, ₹13.6 in FY22, ₹47.8 in FY26) because of large litigation charges in FY21-22 (Ranbaxy-era US cases, Taro price-fixing). On the company's adjusted basis EPS rose from ₹32.0 in FY22 to ₹51.7 in FY26, 12.7% a year, and only 3.5% in FY26 as forex gains, gRevlimid and a low tax rate peaked.

blocks.callout: **The capital question has changed.** For a decade Sun was a cash compounder that bought small specialty assets (Concert, Checkpoint, in-licensing) with surplus cash and paid ~33% of profit as dividends. Organon changes that: ~$2.25 bn of cash plus ~$1.75 bn of new debt for the equity and ~$8 bn of Organon debt taken on, for a business growing −3% to +1% a year. Sun goes from net cash to ~2.3x net debt/EBITDA; the chairman says debt repayment comes first and the dividend policy is not yet decided.

sections.title: Earnings quality: a charge every year, forex inside "EBITDA", a rising tax rate

blocks.p: Four things a reader of Sun's numbers should know. (1) **Exceptional items every year**: litigation (Ranbaxy-era US claims, Taro price-fixing, opioids), impairments of in-licensed assets and restructuring have cost ₹130-950 cr after tax in each of FY23-26 and ₹145 cr in Q1FY27; Organon will add deal and integration costs. The company's "adjusted" EPS excludes them. (2) **Forex gains inside company EBITDA**: Sun's headline FY26 EBITDA of ₹17,731 cr (30.3%) includes a ₹1,240 cr forex gain from the falling rupee; before it, EBITDA was ₹16,491 cr (28.2%). We forecast before forex. (3) **Tax**: the effective rate was 20.2% in FY25 and 23.5% in FY26 (AR note 49, both with one-off items) and 27.8% in Q1FY27 as India tax benefits run out. (4) **Other income** is large (₹1,972 cr in FY26 before forex, ~12% of PBT) and mostly treasury income that will shrink when ~$2.25 bn of cash goes into Organon.

head: Term
What it means
rows: A copy of a medicine whose patent has expired; sold at a fraction of the original price. "Branded generic": a generic sold under a brand name and promoted to doctors (India, emerging markets).
Patented or differentiated branded products (Ilumya, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt, Cequa…) sold at high prices; Sun's name for its specialty business.
US marketing applications for a generic (Abbreviated New Drug Application), a new drug or new formulation (NDA), and a biologic (Biologics License Application).
USFDA, OAI, warning letter, import alert, consent decree

The US regulator; "Official Action Indicated" is its worst inspection outcome; a warning letter lists violations; an import alert blocks shipments from a plant; a consent decree is a court order imposing remedial steps (Ranbaxy, 2012).
Generic lenalidomide (a cancer drug) that several companies sold in limited, agreed volumes in the US from 2022 until full generic entry in Jan-2026: a temporary windfall.
Drug classes: IL-23 blockers treat psoriasis (Ilumya); JAK inhibitors treat alopecia and other immune diseases (Leqselvi); PD-L1 antibodies are cancer immunotherapies (Unloxcyt).
The US government insurance programme that pays for drugs given in a doctor's office or clinic (infusions, injections).
A near-copy of a biologic drug after its patent expires (e.g., Organon's Hadlima, a copy of Humira).
Indian Pharmaceutical Market; Moving Annual Total (last 12 months); AIOCD AWACS (pharmacy sales audit); SMSRC (prescription audit).
A US import duty justified on national-security grounds; for pharma, 100% on patented drugs from 29-Sep-2026 unless a lower rate or exemption applies; generics excluded for now.
Operating profit before depreciation, interest, tax and foreign-exchange gains; Sun's own EBITDA includes forex gains.
Charges or gains the company treats as one-offs (litigation, impairments, restructuring); adjusted EPS excludes them.
Share price divided by the next full financial year's EPS. Sep-28E EPS = half FY28E plus half FY29E (the year ahead of our 12-month target date).
The median premium or discount of pharma peers' P/E on 30-Sep-2026 to their own five-year medians (+10.25%); applied to Sun's own median multiple.
Valuing a company as the sum of separately valued pieces; here standalone Sun on P/E plus the pending Organon deal at cost.
Cost savings or extra sales from combining two companies; Sun expects ~$350 mn of cost synergies from Organon in 2-4 years.
Discounted cash flow; free cash flow to the firm; cost of equity (the return shareholders require: 11.3% here).
Capital work in progress; purchase-price allocation (how an acquisition's price is split into assets, intangibles and goodwill, which sets future amortisation).

India FY27E +14% (Q1 +16%; FY26 +14%; 8.5% market share, +30bp a year; semaglutide since 21-Mar-2026), +12%, +11.5%. US: dollars -4% in FY27E (Q1 $427 mn, -9.7%: gRevlimid gone and more competition in some generics; innovative medicines growing), then +6% a year; rupees +3.5% / +6.3% / +6.0%. methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Sun: P/E on 12-month-forward or FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal 38x 12-month forward, Geojit 30x FY28E, Prabhudas Lilladher 25x FY28E combined-entity EPS; ICICI Securities and Emkay use a sum of the parts). Standalone multiple 29.5x = Sun's median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (26.6x; no trough years) x the pharma sector factor of +10.25% (median of eight peers' P/E vs their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026, excluding Sun; PLAYBOOK §7c) = 29.3x, rounded to the half-turn. The house median on reported EPS is 29.1x (=> 32x, a sensitivity). Organon, still pending on 30-Sep-2026, is valued at what Sun pays (6.2x EBITDA): its base-case part is -26.2 rupees a share (the $2.25 bn of cash that leaves Sun is worth face value, not 29.5x its interest income), so the implied multiple on standalone Sep-28E EPS is 29.08x. Bull 36.5x (75th percentile x factor) plus synergies => 36.73x; bear 24.5x (25th percentile x factor) less a 10% Organon EBITDA shortfall => 23.52x.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 19.5x Sep-28E EBITDA = Sun's 21.3x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 x the +10.25% pharma factor, restated for Sep-28E EBITDA (Rs21,404 cr, before forex) vs the twelve months to Jun-26 on Screener (Rs17,847 cr). Bull 21.5x and bear 17.5x use the 75th and 25th percentiles. Standalone: the Organon part is not added.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether standalone cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash at Mar-27E. Organon is not in it.
